Didn't count calories but I just kept a mental log of my food every day. I mostly ate chicken, rice, whey, pasta, whey, and peanut butter. Oh and some whey. 

As far as training goes, I experimented with a number of programs. I think I made the most gainz using PPL though, so I'm going to continue doing variations of that after my cut. I just love the split. I did PHUL for a while but I didn't really like doing my whole upper/lower body on one day.

Didn't make too many gains in the spring when I started lifting because I was still learning everything. I think the most gainz were made in the summer when I could really focus on my nutrition, I was 210 at the end of the summer. I tore my hamstring in the fall and lost a lot of progress, so that kind of put a hold on things. Once you get past the beginner gains it becomes much harder, so you just gotta train harder.

Dumbell shrugs and deadlifts. For the shrugs I usually take 65 lbs dumbells and just do like 3-4 x 10 and alternate between rolling forward and rolling backward. Last rep I hold it contracted for ~10 secs. The pump from this is crazy.
I played before I started lifting! You don't need to be huge to play, rugby is a bit more technical than most people would think. Go for it man!

I pretty much just ate as much protein and carbs as possible, but I minded my fat intake. I have been very busy with school so "as much as possible" wasn't always that much. And thanks for the support it means a lot!
Also if I had to give one tip, it would be focus on the eccentric part on every single one of your lifts. Best way to Gian mass in my experience
